# Abilities

<!-- Generated by `composer docs:generate` from the operation registry. Do not edit this file: change the declaration and regenerate. -->

SEOCart registers an ability for each operation that declares one, in the ability category `seocart`. An ability runs the same application service as the operation's REST route and WP-CLI command, with the same input schema, permission check and error codes. It is exposed to agents and other clients only when its operation allows it, and an operation that is destructive, moves money or reads personal data in bulk never does.

## `seocart/adjust-stock`

Changes the units on hand of one variant at one location by a signed amount, records the change in the stock ledger with its reason, and returns the stock level after it.

- Operation: `inventory.adjust_stock`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.item_missing` (404), `stock.location_missing` (404), `stock.no_fulfilling_location` (409), `stock.zero_delta` (400), `stock.on_hand_conflict` (409), `stock.adjustment_below_zero` (409), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `variant_id` (required): The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted. An integer of at least 1.
- `location_uuid`: The location whose units change; the store's default location when left out. A deactivated location may still receive units. A uuid.
- `delta` (required): The change of the units on hand: positive for units that arrived, negative for units that left; never 0. An integer from -1000000 to 1000000.
- `reason` (required): Why the units on hand changed. One of `received`, `recount`, `damaged`, `returned`, `correction`.
- `expected_on_hand`: The units on hand the client last read. When given, the change applies only while the variant still has exactly that many, so a repeated request cannot apply it twice. An integer of at least 0.

### Output

- `variant_id` (always): The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted. An integer of at least 1.
- `location_uuid` (always): The location whose units changed. A uuid.
- `on_hand` (always): The units physically in stock after the change. An integer.
- `allocated` (always): The units promised to accepted orders. An integer.
- `held` (always): The units held by checkouts, expired holds included until they are reclaimed. An integer.
- `available` (always): The units that may still be promised: on hand, less allocated, less held. Negative when fewer units were counted than are promised or held. An integer.
- `ledger_entry_id` (always): The id of the stock ledger entry that records the change. An integer.

## `seocart/list-locations`

Lists every location of the store, active or not, in the order orders are routed to them, each with its record, its units on hand and its open allocations.

- Operation: `inventory.list_locations`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403)
- Annotations: readonly `true`, destructive `false`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

This ability takes no input.

### Output

- `locations` (always): The locations, in the order orders are routed to them: ascending priority, ties by the order they were created in. A list of objects, each with `location_uuid`, `name`, `address`, `phone`, `active`, `is_default`, `fulfils_online`, `offers_pickup`, `pickup_ready_in`, `pickup_instructions`, `priority`, `hours`, `units_on_hand`, `open_allocations`. Personal data: returned only to a user who holds the capability `seocart_view_customer_pii`.

## `seocart/create-location`

Creates an active location with its name and, optionally, its address, phone, what it does, its priority and its pickup hours; the store's first location becomes its default.

- Operation: `inventory.create_location`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_settings`
- Error codes: `stock.location_invalid` (400), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `false`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `name` (required): The name the merchant gives the location, such as Main warehouse; not blank. Text of at most 100 characters.
- `address`: Where the location is; given, it replaces the whole address. It is public: it appears on customer-facing documents, such as pickup confirmations, packing slips and shipping labels. An object with `country`, `line1`, `line2`, `city`, `region`, `postcode`.
- `phone`: The location's phone number for the merchant's staff; on a change, an empty text removes it. It is personal data, shown only to a user who may see personal data. Text of at most 32 characters. Personal data.
- `fulfils_online`: Whether the location ships online orders; a new location does unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `offers_pickup`: Whether shoppers may collect orders at the location; a new location does not unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `pickup_ready_in`: How soon a pickup order is usually ready: one of 1h, 2h, next_business_day, 2_4_days. One of `1h`, `2h`, `next_business_day`, `2_4_days`.
- `pickup_instructions`: What a shopper collecting an order is told, such as where to go; it may run over several lines, and on a change an empty text removes it. Text of at most 1000 characters.
- `priority`: Where the location stands when an order is routed: the lowest number is tried first, and locations of the same number in the order they were created; a new location has 0 unless told otherwise. An integer from 0 to 1000000.
- `hours`: The days the location is open for pickup, each day once; given, they replace the location's hours, and a day not listed is closed. A list of 0 to 7 objects, each with `weekday`, `opens_at`, `closes_at`.

### Output

- `location_uuid` (always): The location's public identifier. A uuid.
- `name` (always): The name the merchant gives the location, such as Main warehouse; not blank. Text of at most 100 characters.
- `address` (always): Where the location is, or null until an address is entered. It is public: it appears on customer-facing documents, such as pickup confirmations, packing slips and shipping labels. An object with `country`, `line1`, `line2`, `city`, `region`, `postcode`. May be null.
- `phone`: The location's phone number for the merchant's staff, or null for none. It is personal data, shown only to a user who may see personal data. Text of at most 32 characters. May be null. Personal data: returned only to a user who holds the capability `seocart_view_customer_pii`.
- `active` (always): Whether orders may be routed to the location; an inactive location keeps its stock, and its units are for sale nowhere. True or false.
- `is_default` (always): Whether the location is the store's default: the one an adjustment or an order that names no location uses. True or false.
- `fulfils_online` (always): Whether the location ships online orders; a new location does unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `offers_pickup` (always): Whether shoppers may collect orders at the location; a new location does not unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `pickup_ready_in` (always): How soon a pickup order is usually ready, one of 1h, 2h, next_business_day, 2_4_days, or null when none was given. Text of at most 32 characters. May be null.
- `pickup_instructions` (always): What a shopper collecting an order is told, such as where to go, or null for nothing. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `priority` (always): Where the location stands when an order is routed: the lowest number is tried first, and locations of the same number in the order they were created; a new location has 0 unless told otherwise. An integer from 0 to 1000000.
- `hours` (always): The days the location is open for pickup, by day; a day not listed is closed. A list of 0 to 7 objects, each with `weekday`, `opens_at`, `closes_at`.

## `seocart/deactivate-location`

Deactivates a location: from now on no order is routed to it and its units are for sale nowhere, while its stock stays where it is, or its available units move to another location as one transfer; the default location cannot be deactivated.

- Operation: `inventory.deactivate_location`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_settings`
- Error codes: `stock.location_missing` (404), `stock.location_is_default` (409), `stock.location_inactive` (409), `stock.transfer_same_location` (400), `stock.transfer_state` (409), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `location_uuid` (required): The location to deactivate. A uuid.
- `move_stock_to`: An active location to move the deactivated location's available units to, as one transfer worked in the background; units promised to orders or held by checkouts stay. Moving stock also needs the capability that manages inventory. Repeated with the same location, the deactivation answers the same transfer. Turning the location on again ends the move, the units moved so far staying where they arrived. A uuid.

### Output

- `location_uuid` (always): The location's public identifier. A uuid.
- `name` (always): The name the merchant gives the location, such as Main warehouse; not blank. Text of at most 100 characters.
- `address` (always): Where the location is, or null until an address is entered. It is public: it appears on customer-facing documents, such as pickup confirmations, packing slips and shipping labels. An object with `country`, `line1`, `line2`, `city`, `region`, `postcode`. May be null.
- `phone`: The location's phone number for the merchant's staff, or null for none. It is personal data, shown only to a user who may see personal data. Text of at most 32 characters. May be null. Personal data: returned only to a user who holds the capability `seocart_view_customer_pii`.
- `active` (always): Whether orders may be routed to the location; an inactive location keeps its stock, and its units are for sale nowhere. True or false.
- `is_default` (always): Whether the location is the store's default: the one an adjustment or an order that names no location uses. True or false.
- `fulfils_online` (always): Whether the location ships online orders; a new location does unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `offers_pickup` (always): Whether shoppers may collect orders at the location; a new location does not unless told otherwise. True or false.
- `pickup_ready_in` (always): How soon a pickup order is usually ready, one of 1h, 2h, next_business_day, 2_4_days, or null when none was given. Text of at most 32 characters. May be null.
- `pickup_instructions` (always): What a shopper collecting an order is told, such as where to go, or null for nothing. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `priority` (always): Where the location stands when an order is routed: the lowest number is tried first, and locations of the same number in the order they were created; a new location has 0 unless told otherwise. An integer from 0 to 1000000.
- `hours` (always): The days the location is open for pickup, by day; a day not listed is closed. A list of 0 to 7 objects, each with `weekday`, `opens_at`, `closes_at`.
- `move_transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer that moves the location's available units, or null when no move was asked for. A uuid. May be null.

## `seocart/delete-location`

Deletes a location nothing refers to yet, with its stock items that count nothing; a location with stock history, stock, holds, allocations or transfers is kept, and so is the default location.

- Operation: `inventory.delete_location`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_settings`
- Error codes: `stock.location_missing` (404), `stock.location_in_use` (409), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `location_uuid` (required): The location to delete. A uuid.

### Output

- `location_uuid` (always): The location deleted. A uuid.
- `stock_items_removed` (always): How many of the location's stock items, each holding no units, were deleted with it. An integer.

## `seocart/list-stock`

Lists the stock of up to 200 variants: each one's stock policy, its units at every active location and at any inactive one that still has a stock item, and its units for sale.

- Operation: `inventory.list_stock`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.variant_ids_invalid` (400), `authorization.denied` (403)
- Annotations: readonly `true`, destructive `false`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: yes

### Input

- `variant_ids` (required): The variants, by id: from 1 to 200 whole numbers above 0, separated by commas, such as 12,15,20. A variant with no stock is left out of the answer. Text of at most 4400 characters.

### Output

- `variants` (always): The variants that have stock, by ascending id. A list of objects, each with `variant_id`, `track`, `backorder_policy`, `low_stock_threshold`, `for_sale`, `locations`.

## `seocart/list-transfers`

Lists a page of stock transfers, newest first, each with its lines summed up, filtered by state, by a location they leave or arrive at, or by the order they serve.

- Operation: `inventory.list_transfers`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.location_missing` (404), `authorization.denied` (403)
- Annotations: readonly `true`, destructive `false`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: yes

### Input

- `state`: Only transfers in this state. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `location_uuid`: Only transfers that leave this location or arrive at it. A uuid.
- `order_id`: Only transfers this order waits for. An integer of at least 1.
- `page`: Which page of the list, from 1 to 1000000. An integer from 1 to 1000000. Default `1`.
- `per_page`: How many transfers a page holds, from 1 to 100. An integer from 1 to 100. Default `20`.

### Output

- `transfers` (always): The page of transfers, newest first. A list of objects, each with `transfer_uuid`, `kind`, `state`, `source_location_uuid`, `destination_location_uuid`, `order_id`, `note`, `created_at`, `sent_at`, `received_at`, `lines`, `sent`, `received`, `lost`.
- `page` (always): The page answered. An integer.
- `per_page` (always): How many transfers a page holds. An integer.
- `has_more` (always): Whether a next page has transfers; no total is counted. True or false.

## `seocart/get-transfer`

Returns one stock transfer with its lines: what each sends, what was received and lost, what is on the way, and whether it carries an order's units.

- Operation: `inventory.get_transfer`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.transfer_not_found` (404), `authorization.denied` (403)
- Annotations: readonly `true`, destructive `false`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: yes

### Input

- `transfer_uuid` (required): The transfer. A uuid.

### Output

- `transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer's public identifier. A uuid.
- `kind` (always): Who started the transfer: manual for a merchant's, order for one an order waits for, deactivation for the move of a deactivated location's stock. One of `manual`, `order`, `deactivation`.
- `state` (always): Where the transfer stands: draft, requested, in_transit, received or cancelled. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `source_location_uuid` (always): The location the units leave, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `destination_location_uuid` (always): The location the units arrive at, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `order_id` (always): The order the transfer brings units to, for one of kind order; null otherwise. An integer. May be null.
- `note` (always): The merchant's note on the transfer, such as a tracking number, or null for none. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `created_at` (always): When the transfer was created, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.
- `sent_at` (always): When its units left the source, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until it is sent. Text. May be null.
- `received_at` (always): When its last units were received or written off, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until then. Text. May be null.
- `lines` (always): The transfer's lines, by ascending variant. A list of objects, each with `line_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `received_quantity`, `lost_quantity`, `in_transit`, `allocated`.

## `seocart/create-transfer`

Creates a draft transfer of units from one location to another: it promises nothing, may name more units than the source has, and claims them only when it is sent.

- Operation: `inventory.create_transfer`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.transfer_same_location` (400), `stock.location_missing` (404), `stock.location_inactive` (409), `stock.item_missing` (404), `stock.transfer_invalid` (400), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `false`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `source_location_uuid` (required): The location the units leave; it may be deactivated, so its stock can be moved away. A uuid.
- `destination_location_uuid` (required): The active location the units arrive at, not the source. A uuid.
- `lines` (required): The units to send of each variant, from 1 to 500 lines; lines of one variant are added together. A list of 1 to 500 objects, each with `variant_id`, `quantity`.
- `note`: A note on the transfer, such as why it is made; it may run over several lines. Text of at most 1000 characters.

### Output

- `transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer's public identifier. A uuid.
- `kind` (always): Who started the transfer: manual for a merchant's, order for one an order waits for, deactivation for the move of a deactivated location's stock. One of `manual`, `order`, `deactivation`.
- `state` (always): Where the transfer stands: draft, requested, in_transit, received or cancelled. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `source_location_uuid` (always): The location the units leave, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `destination_location_uuid` (always): The location the units arrive at, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `order_id` (always): The order the transfer brings units to, for one of kind order; null otherwise. An integer. May be null.
- `note` (always): The merchant's note on the transfer, such as a tracking number, or null for none. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `created_at` (always): When the transfer was created, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.
- `sent_at` (always): When its units left the source, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until it is sent. Text. May be null.
- `received_at` (always): When its last units were received or written off, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until then. Text. May be null.
- `lines` (always): The transfer's lines, by ascending variant. A list of objects, each with `line_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `received_quantity`, `lost_quantity`, `in_transit`, `allocated`.

## `seocart/send-transfer`

Sends a draft or requested transfer: every line's units leave the source at once, or, when one line's are not there, none do; until they are received they are on the way, in no location's stock.

- Operation: `inventory.send_transfer`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.transfer_not_found` (404), `stock.transfer_state` (409), `stock.transfer_refused` (409), `stock.transfer_invalid` (400), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `transfer_uuid` (required): The transfer to send. A uuid.
- `note`: A note to keep with the parcel, such as its tracking number; given, it replaces the transfer's note. Text of at most 1000 characters.

### Output

- `transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer's public identifier. A uuid.
- `kind` (always): Who started the transfer: manual for a merchant's, order for one an order waits for, deactivation for the move of a deactivated location's stock. One of `manual`, `order`, `deactivation`.
- `state` (always): Where the transfer stands: draft, requested, in_transit, received or cancelled. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `source_location_uuid` (always): The location the units leave, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `destination_location_uuid` (always): The location the units arrive at, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `order_id` (always): The order the transfer brings units to, for one of kind order; null otherwise. An integer. May be null.
- `note` (always): The merchant's note on the transfer, such as a tracking number, or null for none. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `created_at` (always): When the transfer was created, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.
- `sent_at` (always): When its units left the source, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until it is sent. Text. May be null.
- `received_at` (always): When its last units were received or written off, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until then. Text. May be null.
- `lines` (always): The transfer's lines, by ascending variant. A list of objects, each with `line_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `received_quantity`, `lost_quantity`, `in_transit`, `allocated`.

## `seocart/receive-transfer`

Receives units of a transfer in transit at its destination, line by line, and writes off units lost on the way; the transfer is received once every line's units are received or lost.

- Operation: `inventory.receive_transfer`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.transfer_not_found` (404), `stock.transfer_state` (409), `stock.transfer_receipt_conflict` (409), `stock.transfer_invalid` (400), `stock.item_missing` (404), `stock.location_missing` (404), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `transfer_uuid` (required): The transfer received. A uuid.
- `lines` (required): What arrived of each line, each line once: the units received and lost now, at least one of them, and the units the client last read as received and as lost, so a receipt repeated after a lost answer is refused rather than recorded twice. A list of 1 to 500 objects, each with `line_id`, `received`, `lost`, `expected_received_quantity`, `expected_lost_quantity`.

### Output

- `transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer's public identifier. A uuid.
- `kind` (always): Who started the transfer: manual for a merchant's, order for one an order waits for, deactivation for the move of a deactivated location's stock. One of `manual`, `order`, `deactivation`.
- `state` (always): Where the transfer stands: draft, requested, in_transit, received or cancelled. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `source_location_uuid` (always): The location the units leave, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `destination_location_uuid` (always): The location the units arrive at, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `order_id` (always): The order the transfer brings units to, for one of kind order; null otherwise. An integer. May be null.
- `note` (always): The merchant's note on the transfer, such as a tracking number, or null for none. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `created_at` (always): When the transfer was created, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.
- `sent_at` (always): When its units left the source, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until it is sent. Text. May be null.
- `received_at` (always): When its last units were received or written off, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until then. Text. May be null.
- `lines` (always): The transfer's lines, by ascending variant. A list of objects, each with `line_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `received_quantity`, `lost_quantity`, `in_transit`, `allocated`.

## `seocart/cancel-transfer`

Cancels a draft, or a requested transfer that carries no order's units; a transfer in transit is received or written off instead, never cancelled.

- Operation: `inventory.cancel_transfer`
- Capability: `seocart_manage_inventory`
- Error codes: `stock.transfer_not_found` (404), `stock.transfer_state` (409), `authorization.denied` (403), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `false`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `transfer_uuid` (required): The transfer to cancel. A uuid.

### Output

- `transfer_uuid` (always): The transfer's public identifier. A uuid.
- `kind` (always): Who started the transfer: manual for a merchant's, order for one an order waits for, deactivation for the move of a deactivated location's stock. One of `manual`, `order`, `deactivation`.
- `state` (always): Where the transfer stands: draft, requested, in_transit, received or cancelled. One of `draft`, `requested`, `in_transit`, `received`, `cancelled`.
- `source_location_uuid` (always): The location the units leave, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `destination_location_uuid` (always): The location the units arrive at, or null when it no longer exists. A uuid. May be null.
- `order_id` (always): The order the transfer brings units to, for one of kind order; null otherwise. An integer. May be null.
- `note` (always): The merchant's note on the transfer, such as a tracking number, or null for none. Text of at most 1000 characters. May be null.
- `created_at` (always): When the transfer was created, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.
- `sent_at` (always): When its units left the source, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until it is sent. Text. May be null.
- `received_at` (always): When its last units were received or written off, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond; null until then. Text. May be null.
- `lines` (always): The transfer's lines, by ascending variant. A list of objects, each with `line_id`, `variant_id`, `quantity`, `received_quantity`, `lost_quantity`, `in_transit`, `allocated`.

## `seocart/refund-order`

Gives back units of an order's lines, and what is left of its shipping when asked, through the gateway its payment was taken by, at the order's own rate, and answers the refund; the Idempotency-Key header is required, and a retry with the same key and the same request is answered with the same refund, never a second one.

- Operation: `payment.refund_order`
- Capability: `seocart_refund_orders`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403), `order.not_found` (404), `payment.refund_key_missing` (400), `payment.refund_key_reused` (422), `payment.refund_request_invalid` (422), `payment.refund_note_rejected` (422), `payment.refund_not_refundable` (409), `payment.gateway_unavailable` (503), `payment.operation_unsupported` (409), `payment.unreconciled` (409), `payment.refund_unresolved` (409), `payment.refund_line_not_found` (404), `payment.refund_line_exhausted` (409), `payment.refund_exceeds_captured` (409), `payment.refund_nothing_left` (409), `payment.refund_cap_exceeded` (403), `payment.refund_retry` (409), `payment.refund_declined` (402), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `order_uuid` (required): The public identifier of the order to refund. A uuid.
- `lines`: The units of each line to give back, each line at most once; may be empty only when the shipping is asked for. A list of 0 to 200 objects, each with `line_uuid`, `quantity`, `restock`.
- `shipping`: Whether to give back what is left of the order's shipping; when absent, it is not given back. True or false.
- `reason_code` (required): Why the order is refunded. One of `customer_return`, `damaged`, `not_as_described`, `late_delivery`, `duplicate_order`, `fraud`, `goodwill`, `other`.
- `note`: What the person who refunds writes about the refund; kept with it, and refused when it holds a card number. Text of at most 500 characters. Personal data.
- `idempotency_key`: The request's idempotency key, sent in the Idempotency-Key header and nowhere else, of at most 64 bytes: a new key, such as a UUID, for each new request, and the same key when that request is retried. Text of at most 64 characters.

### Output

- `refund_uuid` (always): The refund's public identifier, which the gateway received as its idempotency key. A uuid.
- `order_uuid` (always): The order refunded. A uuid.
- `total_minor` (always): What the refund gave back, tax included, in minor units of the order's currency. An integer.
- `tax_minor` (always): The tax the refund gave back, in minor units of the order's currency. An integer.
- `shipping_minor` (always): The shipping the refund gave back, before tax, in minor units of the order's currency. An integer.
- `currency` (always): The order's currency, ISO 4217. Text of at most 3 characters.
- `base_total_minor` (always): The total in minor units of the base currency, at the order's own rate. An integer.
- `base_currency` (always): The store's base currency when the order was placed, ISO 4217. Text of at most 3 characters.
- `reason_code` (always): Why the order was refunded. Text.
- `note`: What the person who refunds writes about the refund; kept with it, and refused when it holds a card number. Text of at most 500 characters. Personal data: returned only to a user who holds the capability `seocart_view_customer_pii`.
- `lines` (always): The units of each line the refund was asked for, in the order of the lines' identifiers. A list of objects, each with `line_uuid`, `quantity`, `restock`.

## `seocart/settle-refund-claim`

Ends the claim of a refund the payment gateway could not account for, on a person's say-so: the gateway is asked once more, and a refund it made or declined is recorded as it says; only when it cannot say does the statement decide, a refund stated made being recorded with the provider's refund and the amount it names and the order flagged for a person, and one stated not made ending declined with nothing recorded. A claim that has ended is refused, so a retry is safe.

- Operation: `payment.settle_refund_claim`
- Capability: `seocart_override_money_state`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403), `payment.refund_note_rejected` (422), `payment.refund_statement_incomplete` (422), `payment.refund_claim_not_found` (404), `payment.refund_claim_ended` (409), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `refund_uuid` (required): The public identifier of the refund whose claim is settled. A uuid.
- `statement` (required): What the person states: refunded, when the payment provider gave the money back, or not_refunded, when it did not. The gateway's own answer, when it has one, decides instead. One of `refunded`, `not_refunded`.
- `provider_refund_id`: The payment provider's refund, as its dashboard names it: required with refunded, refused with not_refunded. Text of at most 191 characters.
- `amount_minor`: What the provider gave back, in minor units of the order's currency: required with refunded, refused with not_refunded. An integer of at least 1.
- `note` (required): Why the person states it; kept with the claim, and refused when it holds a card number. Text of at most 500 characters. Personal data.

### Output

- `refund_uuid` (always): The refund whose claim was settled. A uuid.
- `order_uuid` (always): The order refunded. A uuid.
- `state` (always): How the claim ended: recorded, the refund recorded; declined, no money given back, so the same refund asked again is a new one; or unreconciled, money left for a person to reconcile. Text.
- `decided_by` (always): What decided how the claim ended: gateway, when the payment gateway made or declined the refund, or statement, when it could not say and the person's statement decided. Text.
- `gateway_reading` (always): What the payment gateway said when it was asked once more: approved, declined, not_found, cannot_say, or unavailable, with why after a colon when known, such as unavailable:not_registered. Text.
- `has_unreconciled_money` (always): Whether the order holds money a person must reconcile now: true after a refund recorded on a person's statement, until a person clears it. True or false.

## `seocart/clear-unreconciled-money`

Lowers the flag of an order holding money a person must reconcile, with the note saying why, once a person has reconciled that money; a payment result the plugin could not apply that is older than the clearance then no longer holds the order's refunds back. An order not flagged is refused, so a retry is safe.

- Operation: `order.clear_unreconciled_money`
- Capability: `seocart_override_money_state`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403), `order.reconciliation_note_rejected` (422), `order.not_found` (404), `order.not_unreconciled` (409), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `order_uuid` (required): The public identifier of the order whose unreconciled money is cleared. A uuid.
- `note` (required): Why the person says the order's money is reconciled; kept with the order, and refused when it holds a card number. Text of at most 500 characters. Personal data.

### Output

- `order_uuid` (always): The order whose unreconciled money was cleared. A uuid.
- `has_unreconciled_money` (always): Whether the order holds money a person must reconcile: false once cleared. True or false.
- `money_reconciled_at` (always): When the flag was cleared, UTC, in ISO 8601 to the microsecond, by the database clock. Text.

## `seocart/capture-payment`

Captures an authorized payment through its gateway, everything authorized or, where the gateway declares partial captures, the amount given, the gateway releasing the rest; a payment is captured once, so a capture asked again after it was made is refused with payment.not_capturable and what was captured, and one whose answer was lost is asked again with the same request, which the gateway carries out once.

- Operation: `payment.capture_payment`
- Capability: `seocart_capture_payments`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403), `payment.intent_not_found` (404), `payment.not_capturable` (409), `payment.unreconciled` (409), `payment.capture_exceeds_authorized` (409), `payment.operation_unsupported` (409), `payment.gateway_unavailable` (503), `payment.gateway_no_answer` (502), `payment.operation_declined` (402), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `intent_uuid` (required): The public identifier of the payment, as its order's payment record names it. A uuid.
- `amount_minor`: What to capture, in minor units of the payment's currency: at most what was authorized, and less only where the payment's gateway declares partial captures; when absent, everything authorized. An integer of at least 1.

### Output

- `intent_uuid` (always): The public identifier of the payment, as its order's payment record names it. A uuid.
- `outcome` (always): applied, or duplicate when another request had made the same capture or void a moment before. One of `applied`, `duplicate`.
- `status` (always): The payment's status now. One of `created`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `authorized`, `captured`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `voided`, `failed`.
- `payment_status` (always): How far the payment's order is paid now. One of `unpaid`, `pending`, `authorized`, `partially_paid`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `voided`, `failed`, `disputed`, `terms_pending`.
- `amount_minor` (always): What the gateway captured, or released for a void, in minor units of the payment's currency. An integer.
- `currency` (always): The payment's currency, ISO 4217. Text of at most 3 characters.

## `seocart/void-payment`

Voids an authorized payment through its gateway, releasing what it authorized before anything is captured, for a declared reason; an order still waiting for its payment is cancelled, and an order accepted is left to the person who voids it; a captured payment is never voided, but refunded, and a void asked again after it was made is refused with payment.not_voidable.

- Operation: `payment.void_payment`
- Capability: `seocart_void_payments`
- Error codes: `authorization.denied` (403), `payment.intent_not_found` (404), `payment.not_voidable` (409), `payment.unreconciled` (409), `payment.operation_unsupported` (409), `payment.gateway_unavailable` (503), `payment.gateway_no_answer` (502), `payment.operation_declined` (402), `store.unavailable` (503)
- Annotations: readonly `false`, destructive `true`, idempotent `true`
- Exposed to agents: no

### Input

- `intent_uuid` (required): The public identifier of the payment, as its order's payment record names it. A uuid.
- `reason` (required): Why the payment is voided. One of `customer_request`, `duplicate_order`, `fraud`, `out_of_stock`, `other`.

### Output

- `intent_uuid` (always): The public identifier of the payment, as its order's payment record names it. A uuid.
- `outcome` (always): applied, or duplicate when another request had made the same capture or void a moment before. One of `applied`, `duplicate`.
- `status` (always): The payment's status now. One of `created`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `authorized`, `captured`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `voided`, `failed`.
- `payment_status` (always): How far the payment's order is paid now. One of `unpaid`, `pending`, `authorized`, `partially_paid`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `voided`, `failed`, `disputed`, `terms_pending`.
- `amount_minor` (always): What the gateway captured, or released for a void, in minor units of the payment's currency. An integer.
- `currency` (always): The payment's currency, ISO 4217. Text of at most 3 characters.
